item.title: Feature: Why Didn't Rockstar Use FSR 4 on Series X for GTA 6? Microsoft's Stats Have the Answer
item.description:
Plus: why does the base PS5 version not use QSSR?

A common question we've seen online in the wake of GTA 6 reviews going live is the conundrum over the Xbox Series X. The game renders at an internal resolution of 1440p, with an in-house TAA upscale to 4K. Why didn't Rockstar use the recently-released FSR 4 AI upscaler instead, as they did on Xbox Series S? Come to think of it, why didn't they use Sony's QSSR on base PS5 too?

Let's tackle the Series X question first. Here, the answer may be hiding in plain sight - after all, Microsoft published the critical FSR 4 stats for Xbox developers just earlier this month. And within those figures, you can see that the frame-time cost of FSR 4, both the full-fat (3.86ms) and lite (2.75ms) versions, is likely to be significantly higher than the cost of Rockstar's in-house TAA.

item.title: Review: Grand Theft Auto 6: A Landmark Achievement That Redefines a Console Generation
item.description:
Even more impressive than we expected - despite performance compromises.

Grand Theft Auto 6 marks a pivotal technical milestone for Rockstar Games, delivering arguably the most detailed, dense and convincing recreation of an urban environment yet seen in interactive media. Built entirely from the ground up for modern hardware, the sprawling depiction of Vice City and its surrounding state of Leonida leaves behind the generational compromises that constrained its predecessor. The result is an extraordinary simulation where sheer scale matches an obsessive attention to minute visual detail.
